content.title: Iberia
History Outnumbered

modules.quote: To commemorate the 80th anniversary of the Holocaust and Canal Historia's 25th anniversary, Dentsu Creative Iberia launched "History Outnumbered." At a time when data is used to distort reality, we used it to restore it. This poignant campaign juxtaposes the tattooed numbers of Holocaust survivors with contemporary hate crime statistics, delivering a stark warning: if we don't learn from history, we're doomed to repeat it.

content.text: In an era where far-right extremism and hate crimes are alarmingly on the rise, Canal Historia faced the challenge of making historical lessons resonate with today's audience. The goal was to create a campaign that not only commemorated past atrocities but also highlighted their relevance in today's societal context.
Bridging Past and Present Through Visual Storytelling

Dentsu Creative Iberia employed a minimalist yet powerful visual strategy. By overlaying contemporary hate statistics onto images of Holocaust survivors' tattooed numbers, the campaign created a chilling parallel between historical atrocities and current events. This approach served as a visceral reminder of the consequences of unchecked hatred. And while it doesn’t solve extremism, it does something equally powerful: it makes denial impossible.

The campaign launched across TV, print, and out-of-home platforms, featuring stark visuals that combined survivors' tattoos with present-day hate crime data. Headlines like "33,963 Racial Hate Crimes in Germany in 2024" and "1,856 Likes on the comment 'We miss you, Hitler'" were superimposed over these images, creating a powerful narrative that history's darkest chapters are at risk of repeating. In a time of rising extremism, it gave Canal Historia a campaign that hit where it mattered, public spaces, mass media, and minds.

content.title: Improbable Housemates

modules.quote: We worked with MEO to launch "Improbable Housemates" a campaign and platform that          helped unlock the housing crisis in Portugal.

content.text: Portugal is facing a dramatic housing crisis as a result of several factors: decades of frozen rents, tourism and local rental boom, special policies for immigrants, as well as rampant inflation and low average salaries.

House prices have become prohibitive - a problem that particularly affects 120,000 young university students and the 500,000 seniors living alone in large houses, in deep loneliness. These were two structural problems to which MEO, the country's largest telecom operator, decided to draw attention with an innovative Christmas campaign.

image.alt: Improbable Housemates Ana Rosa 85 years old matched with Marina Santos 20 years old

meta_data.alt: Improbable Housemates Ana Rosa 85 years old matched with Marina Santos 20 years old

image.alt: Improbable Housemates Ana and Marina sit on sofa

meta_data.alt: Improbable Housemates Ana and Marina sit on sofa

content.text: MEO, the top Portuguese Telecom has always been a brand of causes, believing it has a responsibility to give back to society. Its communication has always been about people, so it chose to target two key vulnerable groups in the country - students and elderly people. As the Christmas holidays is the peak season for brand advertising, Meo wanted to stand out from the competition with an unifying message that aimed to raise awareness of the problem.

images.alt: Improbable Housemates student cooks dinner for elderly housemate

meta_data.alt: Improbable Housemates student cooks dinner for elderly housemate

images.alt: Improbable Housemates girl sits on bed

meta_data.alt: Improbable Housemates girl sits on bed

images.alt: Improbable Housemates photos from elderly housemate's youth

meta_data.alt: Improbable Housemates photos from elderly housemate's youth

content.text: WHEN A DOOR OPENS, A HEART OPENS TOO

We designed a national digital platform that that brought together young students with elderly people who live alone. Taking full advantage of the holiday spirit, what seemed like a typical Christmas campaign was the pretext for launching a platform with an emotional story. Directed by the Oscar-nominated director Marco Martins, we told the story of a student who travels far from home to go to university and shares a house with an elderly woman. Set to Sia's “Angel by the wings”, the film shows their relationship evolve from purely practical into a strong friendship, climaxing with the girl surprising the elderly on Christmas Eve by taking her to ice skating. This beautiful story shows two generations coming together, ending with the line: “When a door opens, a heart opens too”.

content.title: Easy Reading

modules.quote: Bringing content accessibility for all one step closer to reality.

meta_data.alt: Kindle with Easy Reading

content.text: According to the world tourism organization, the numbers of travellers are almost back to normal following the outbreak of Covid-19. But 40 million people with intellectual disabilities across the globe are still shut out. How could Visit Portugal make its cities, stories, traditions and authors accessible to all?

image.alt: Happy man using AI reading tool on kindle

meta_data.alt: Happy man using AI reading tool on kindle

content.text: In 2020, in the midst of lockdown and with the country's borders closed due to the pandemic, Visit Portugal launched Read Portugal, a campaign where people could "continue to visit" the Portuguese country by reading its literary classics. It was an initiative to open the country to the world, but how could we take it further to make Portugal truly open to all?

meta_data.alt: Person reading

image.alt: Happy man in library with kindle

meta_data.alt: Happy man in library with kindle

content.text: We created an articifical intellience tool capable of combining text processing with the creation of images to convert any novel into an "easy-to-read" book.  This AI tool has been trained following the European standards for making information Easy-to-Read and makes Portuguese literature accessible to people with intellectual disabilities. It reads and synthesizes the original text, simplifying and replacing complex words and rephrasing content into shorter sentences. Additionally, it automatically generates illustrations in order to provide context, while formatting the information following design rules that enhance readability. Then an expert in Easy-to-Read validates the content. By digitizing much of the work that has been done manually the past, making it highly time-consuming and costly, "translating" text to make it accessible can be done at speed and scale. Now, with Easy Reading, millions of books, have the potential to be read by everyone.

content.title: The Jewel Inside

modules.quote: Dentsu Creative Iberia worked with Heinz to design a piece of jewelry specifically to break a chef's number one rule: no ketchup allowed.

content.text: Spain is a country where gastronomy is highly respected. With more than 270 Michelin-starred restaurants, some of the world's best chefs, and a culture that venerates food as if it were a religion, the culinary scene is exceptional.

However, times are changing, and every day there are more Heinz ketchup fans who are eager to add a touch of their favorite condiment to the most prestigious dishes. The problem? In these restaurants, ketchup is frowned upon.

image.alt: The Jewel Inside Heinz Ketchup Ring

meta_data.alt: The Jewel Inside Heinz Ketchup Ring

content.text: Asking for ketchup in a luxury restaurant is quite a risk. Not only can they deny it to you, but you might even offend the chef. And in Spain this poses a significant problem for Heinz lovers. Aligned with Heinz's global strategy, we needed to create a campaign that would generate a lot of buzz... A campaign that would leave Ferran Adria, Arzak, or Dabiz Muñoz (some of the most famous Spanish chefs in the world) speechless.

images.alt: The Jewel Inside Heinz Ketchup Ring Design

meta_data.alt: The Jewel Inside Heinz Ketchup Ring Design

images.alt: The Jewel Inside Heinz Ketchup Ring Design

meta_data.alt: The Jewel Inside Heinz Ketchup Ring Design

images.alt: The Jewel Inside Heinz Ketchup Ring Design

meta_data.alt: The Jewel Inside Heinz Ketchup Ring Design

content.text: We invented a wearable solution that allows people to sneak Heinz into places without being discovered: by creating the first ring that conceals and dispenses ketchup. It's a piece of jewelry designed specifically to be worn with class while breaking the chef's number one rule: no ketchup allowed.

It is replenished with specially designed biodegradable Heinz ketchup capsules. Each one provides a single dose of the product, enough to turn a simple dish into the most delightful one. For the manufacturing of The Jewel Inside, we enlisted the help of a team of industrial engineers to create a 3d printed prototype, and the final pieces of jewelry were crafted by silversmiths using sterling silver.
The custom-made ketchup capsules are also biodegradable and safe for food consumption and it took over three months to achieve a functional product for the campaign.

content.title: THE UNIMAGINABLE RETURN

modules.quote: The avant-garde electronic music festival, Jardim Sonoro, turned visual AI platform’s flaws into its 2022 edition artwork.

image.alt: Marketing campaign for avant-garde electronic music festival, Jardim Sonoro.

content.text: In 2022 Jardim Sonoro, an avant-garde, artistically and identitarily differentiated electronic music festival in Portugal, would make its comeback in a physical format after two years of pandemic, deepening its roots in an even more natural location.

This edition had plenty of news to communicate. Jardim Sonoro flourished with a new concept 'Blended with nature' and camouflaged and merged even deeper in nature, moving its ground to Monsanto, the lung of Lisbon, reconnecting the city and its people with nature.
We had to imagine and deliver the campaign for this new Jardim Sonoro, taking these transformations and its reinforced concept into account.
BLENDING ARTISTS WITH NATURE USING AI
To imagine and conceive a new campaign for Jardim Sonoro, now placed in a new forest venue, merged even deeper in nature, became a hard task.

Assuming and remembering that great masterpieces are often born from error, we took advantage of the erratic interpretations of visual AI platforms so we could explore its flaws transforming them into something unique.
We challenged the machine to give it a try and imagine the new Jardim Sonoro for us.

Artists were blended with nature, featuring their most prominent characteristics whilst machine learning and art direction worked side by side, calibrating the search for the perfect prompts and the more exquisite outputs.
The results were everything we never expected or imagined.

content.title: THE FORGOTTEN TEAM

modules.quote: A forgotten team, and its yellow jersey aimed to raise awareness of the Qatar World Cup human rights abuses and raise funds for the victims' families.

content.text: MEO, Portugal's top broadcaster and official sponsor of the national 2022 Qatar World Cup team, faced a dilemma.
Dentsu Creative partnered with Amnesty International to form the “Forgotten Team", to raise awareness about human rights abuse and raise funds for the victims' families.

The team jersey was inspired by the workers' vests, in electric yellow complete with reflective bands and the number 4 representing Article 4 of the Human Rights Act on the back, with a QR code to drive donations.

Jerseys were distributed at football stadiums with the objective to create a symbol that would unite fans to support the cause, and distinctly stand out amongst the colourful and celebratory crowds at games.

image.alt: The Forgotten Team - high vis team shirt

content.text: A SYMBOL OF BRAVERY AND VIRTUE
When football authorities banned the jersey from stadiums, it soon went on to become a symbol of bravery and virtue and ignited a rallying spirit.
The impact on the Portuguese people was immense, with the abuses in Qatar so close to the heart of a nation with many immigrants and overseas workers.

The campaign reached 98% of Portugal with more than 1.5M of earned media. It was the highest evaluated World Cup campaign with 78% approval rating, surpassing the evaluations of big sport, alcohol and fast food brands who sponsored.
The Forgotten Team continues to send jerseys to future World Cup hosts in an effort to ensure that workers' rights are not forgotten.
It showed that a brand can stand for something more than just profits, and that people will support those who take a stand for what they believe in.

values.description: Voted Most Impactful World Cup Campaign by 78% in SCOPE survey

content.text: Dentsu Brand Spaces es la unidad especializada en experiencia de marca y diseño de espacios de Dentsu Creative España.
Ayudamos a las marcas a transformar su estrategia y posicionamiento en experiencias físicas relevantes, creando espacios que expresan quiénes son y qué representan.

Diseñamos entornos donde la marca se vive, no solo se comunica. Desde oficinas, espacios retail y shop-in-shops hasta flagships y experiencias de marca, convertimos cada decisión de diseño en una oportunidad para reforzar la identidad, la cultura y la conexión con las personas.

Nuestro enfoque parte siempre de la estrategia de marca: entendemos primero qué debe transmitir una compañía y después lo traducimos en materiales, recorridos, ambientes e interacciones que generan experiencias coherentes y memorables.
Porque cuando el espacio y la marca hablan el mismo idioma, el diseño deja de ser únicamente estética y se convierte en una herramienta de negocio.
